$comment: FAMILY KNOWLEDGE for the RERANKER role, keyed by the model id the packaging
step wrote into resources/rerankers/<org>/<model>/. The sibling of
models/spaces.json, and the same argument: a model absent from this file is
refused loudly rather than scored under guessed settings.
Two settings live here because neither is in the model's own files and both
change what the number MEANS:
truncationSide  which half of an over-long (query, passage) pair loses
tokens. The same passage scored under `only_second` and
under a balanced strategy is two different scores, and
neither config.json nor tokenizer_config.json says which
the caller gets. MEASURED, not assumed: this said
`longest_first` until a probe encoded real pairs and read
the [SEP] positions back. transformers.js keeps the head
of the CONCATENATED sequence — a 400/400 pair kept all 400
query tokens and cut the passage, and a 600-token query
left no separator at all. This string is part of the
identity HASH, so correcting it changes the reranker's
fingerprint and every score stored under the false
description is correctly treated as a different
measurement and recomputed.
scoreSemantics  what the stored number IS. This head emits ONE raw logit;
we record sigmoid(logit) beside it for readability, and
the pair is never a calibrated probability. Rank it, never
threshold it. If a later decision stores something else
under the same column, that is a different measurement and
the identity hash must move with it.
Everything else — the weights' sha256, the quantisation, the maximum
sequence length — is derived from the bytes on disk, so swapping the
packaged model changes the identity without anyone editing a constant.

cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2.source: https://huggingface.co/cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 — trained on MS MARCO over (query, passage) pairs; the model card's usage example sorts by the RAW logit and applies no softmax.
